findings.problem: S-1 says the status request 'carries no credential', but no test covers that half. The guard `credentials: 'omit'` (src/main/ollama-locality.ts:54) can be deleted and all 34 locality tests still pass. Node's fetch never sends cookies or ambient auth, so the 'bare GET: no credential, no cookie' test (tests/ollama-locality.test.ts:173-182) cannot fail on this. In production the guard matters: Electron 44.4.5 net.fetch turns a default 'same-origin' request with no Origin header into credentials 'include', which sends the local session's cookies and HTTP auth.
findings.evidence: Mutation H (removed `credentials: 'omit'` from the fetch init at ollama-locality.ts:54): SURVIVED, 34/34 passed. The U2 guard-proof table pins this test only with 'Authorization header injected (G16)'. Electron 44.4.5 binary (node_modules/electron/dist/electron), fetchWithSession: `u="same-origin"!==c.credentials||d?c.credentials:"include"` and then `request({...,credentials:u,...,redirect:c.redirect})`. The same code confirms `redirect:'error'` kills the request: `_die(new Error("Attempted to redirect, but redirect policy was 'error'"))`. Electron's Response is built with `new Response(...)`, so `response.redirected` is always false there, and `redirect:'error'` is the only working redirect guard in production.

findings.problem: Under some conditions the fail-closed locality check is answered from Electron's HTTP cache instead of by Ollama, so it does not actually run before every step (F-6). readStatus calls `localSession.fetch(url, { method: 'GET', redirect: 'error', credentials: 'omit', signal })` and sets no `cache` mode. If the /api/status answer carries a freshness header (Cache-Control max-age, Expires, or only Last-Modified, which gets heuristic freshness), the session cache (the in-memory 'moonaliza-local' partition, alive for the whole app session) serves the old `cloud.disabled: true` on later steps and later runs. If Ollama is restarted with cloud on in between, the check still passes and the chat request goes out, so the prompt can reach ollama.com under a local-only policy. That is the case design point (b) gives as its reason for checking every step rather than at profile save. Precondition: stock Ollama's StatusHandler (E-31 capture lines 2211-2218, gin `c.JSON`) sets none of these headers, so a bare Ollama is not affected. A server in front of it that adds them is affected, and the spec supports endpoints with a path. The unit tests cannot see this because they use Node's fetch, which has no HTTP cache.

findings.problem: The status connection can stay open after the refusal. This happens when the fetcher ignores the signal, the response headers arrive after the 5 s bound, and the body never ends. readStatus reaches `signal.addEventListener('abort', cancel, { once: true })` with a signal that has already aborted, so the listener never fires. The read loop does not check `signal.aborted`, so it reads forever. The refusal itself still arrives on time through untilAborted. The existing test 'a run cancelled while the status body is still arriving closes the connection, even through a fetcher that ignores the signal' covers only the case where headers arrive before the abort. The production fetcher (Electron session.fetch) honours the signal, and in Electron both the silent and stalled servers had their sockets closed. So this is a defensive gap only.

findings.problem: Pre-existing, not introduced by b793f13..f1c4867. lines() splits only on `\r?\n`, but the SSE grammar that readSseEvents now follows also allows a lone CR as a line end. A CR-framed stream therefore arrives as one line. If it begins with OpenRouter's comment, the whole stream, data and [DONE] included, is skipped as a single comment. The call then ends `incomplete` with empty content, the run fails with PROVIDER_ERROR, and an empty partial message is kept. A CR-framed stream that starts with `data:` fails with PROVIDER_INVALID_RESPONSE. No vendor in the corpus uses lone CR.

findings.problem: Pre-existing, in lines(), unchanged by this diff, but on the readSseEvents path. Every chunk appends to `pending` and re-splits the whole buffer, so parsing a long event is quadratic in the number of chunks. findings.problem: S-1 says the status request carries no credential, but no test covers the `credentials: 'omit'` guard in readStatus (src/main/ollama-locality.ts:54). If someone removes it, the whole suite stays green. In production, removing it would send the local session's cookies and cached HTTP auth with GET /api/status. The test 'the status request is a bare GET: no credential, no cookie, ...' cannot fail on this guard because it runs through Node's global fetch, which has no cookie jar and no auth cache. T-1 (every guard shown red) is also not met for this guard.
findings.evidence: Electron 44.4.5 fetchWithSession, read from node_modules/electron/dist/electron, does: `d=c.headers.get("origin")??void 0, u="same-origin"!==c.credentials||d?c.credentials:"include"` and then `credentials:u`. Without the explicit 'omit', the Request default 'same-origin' with no Origin header becomes 'include', so the request carries the session's cookies and HTTP auth. Cookies are scoped by host, not port, so a cookie set by any other 127.0.0.1 server would reach Ollama. ClientRequest docs (electron.d.ts:21056-21065): 'If set to include, credentials from the session associated with the request will be used.'

findings.problem: How a non-object `error` field is treated is unpinned. Mutation S02 (`.error != null` -> `.error !== undefined`) would fail every call from a vendor that sends `"error": null` on normal chunks. Mutation S03 (`.error != null` -> `.error`, truthy) would accept `"error": false`, `""` or `0`. Both survive.
findings.evidence: src/main/provider-stream.ts:158 `if (typeof raw === 'object' && raw !== null && (raw as { error?: unknown }).error != null) throw new Error('PROVIDER_STREAM_ERROR');`. No captured vendor stream shows either shape, so the effect stays hypothetical.

findings.fix: Optional: a test where an E-20 chunk carrying `"error": null` still completes, which pins the `!= null` choice.

findings.problem: Two SSE grammar edge cases are unpinned. Mutation S07 (`event = value || undefined` -> `event = value`) makes an empty `event:` line yield the name ''. Mutation S11 (`colon === -1 ? line : ...` -> `colon === -1 ? '' : ...`) ignores a colon-less `data` line, which the SSE grammar reads as an empty data value. Both survive.
findings.evidence: src/main/provider-stream.ts:67 (S11) and :69 (S07). No vendor capture sends either form.
findings.reproduction: Apply S07 or S11 and run the 4 related files: green.
findings.fix: Optional grammar tests. Low value until a vendor shows either form.

findings.reproduction: Apply S18 and run the 4 related files: green.
findings.fix: Either test readSse with a small maxBytes expecting PROVIDER_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE, or drop the unused parameter.

findings.reproduction: Apply L21 and run the 4 related files: green.
